content_type: live gameplay commentary -- high-energy delivery, frequent mid-sentence pauses, code-switched speech
description: A starting point for fast commentary. Differs from example_tutorial in two deliberate ways: the duration ceiling is DISABLED, and the timing bias is ZERO. Both were wrong when inherited from a calmer profile. Read the notes before changing anything.

transcription._warning: DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- nothing reads this block. The real flags live in the streamer profile's `whisper` block.
transcription.language: set this explicitly -- whisper.cpp defaults to 'en' and will TRANSLATE other languages rather than transcribe them
transcription._word_timestamps_note: Required: make_captions.py reads transcript['transcription'] as whisper's SEGMENT list, and it only yields one word per entry because these flags force one word per segment.
transcription.dtw: medium -- strongly recommended; feeds the align stage
transcription.vad: silero -- strongly recommended; see align in the streamer profile

line_grouping._note: A low pause threshold can produce short orphan cues (a single trailing word on its own line). Raising it to ~300 ms barely changed output on the content this was measured on, because punctuation and max_chars dominate. Measure before tuning.

repeated_word_handling.note: Consecutive identical words within this gap merge into one cue.

duration_ceiling._note: DISABLED BY SENTINEL -- 99.0 means the cap is never reached. This is deliberate. A per-word ceiling carried over from calmer content was the dominant defect on fast commentary: it truncated 13 of 84 cues and left captions covering only 105 s of a 180 s clip with 13 holes over a second. Disabling it restored 179 s of coverage and removed every hole. The correct long-term fix is a per-word plausibility clamp, not a blanket ceiling.

timing_bias_correction._note: ZEROED DELIBERATELY, which is NOT the same as measured-as-zero. These are whisper's raw timestamps. Carrying a measured shift over from different content compressed every cue and pushed the shortest to 0.11 s. Getting a real number requires a hand-corrected SRT for one stretch of your own footage. Until you have that, leave these at zero.

post_processing.note: No line's end may exceed the next line's start.
post_processing._spread_collapsed_note: ON here. When whisper stamps several words with one identical timestamp, the resulting cue would collapse to start == end and never appear on screen. With this on, those lines share the available span proportionally by text length instead. Leave it on unless you are reproducing a fixture.

known_limitations: NO SILENCE GATING at the caption stage -- the main open defect. Whisper stretches a word's timestamp across adjacent silence (a two-syllable word can span 1.9 s), so with the ceiling disabled captions tile the whole timeline and linger through silence. The align stage (DTW + Silero VAD, see streamers/example.json) mitigates this upstream and is the reason this profile is usable at all; run it. No parameter in THIS file can fix it.
Timing bias is unmeasured -- see timing_bias_correction.
Rapid repeated-word stretches may merge into one longer cue rather than matching manually-split rhythm.
Short orphan cues can appear at low pause thresholds.
_status: STARTING POINT, not a validated profile. Measured by eye on a timeline rather than diffed against a manual reference edit. Treat the numbers as defaults to measure against your own footage, not as correct values.
